items.statement:
Assume full AC. If $F_0,F_1\subset S^3$ are compact smooth embedded spanning surfaces for the same nonempty link, with no closed components but allowing disconnectedness and nonorientability, then
$$\nu(B_{F_0})+c(F_0)-1=\nu(B_{F_1})+c(F_1)-1.$$
Here $B_F$ is the full rational normal-transfer pairing, including its cross-component entries, $\nu(B_F)$ is the dimension of its kernel, and $c(F)$ is its number of connected components. The quantity is invariant under orientation-preserving ambient isotopy of the boundary link.

Consequently any two such surfaces whose full normal-transfer pairings are nondegenerate have the same number of components. In particular this holds for two definite surfaces of either sign, including opposite signs. If $F_0,F_1$ are definite spanning surfaces for the same link, and proper arcs $\alpha_0\subset F_0$, $\alpha_1\subset F_1$ have the property that their cut surfaces span ambient isotopic links, then $\alpha_0$ separates its surface component if and only if $\alpha_1$ does. This last assertion concerns separation, without asserting an alternating diagram or identifying the number of split components of the link.

citations.quote: Assume countable choice. Every connected compact smooth surface $F$ with nonempty boundary has a finite smooth disk-and-band presentation: it is diffeomorphic, respecting its actual boundary parametrization, to finitely many smooth disks with finitely many rectangular bands attached along pairs of disjoint boundary intervals, with compatible corner rounding. Equivalently it has a finite handle decomposition with only zero- and one-handles, all zero-handles first. The assertion allows nonorientable surfaces and twisted bands. For a smoothly embedded surface these data may be transported to the actual surface, so its disk, band and attaching charts are supplied inside that surface, rather than merely as a homotopy type.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, every component of which has nonempty boundary. The ambient sphere has its standard orientation. The normal-transfer expression $B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a symmetric integral bilinear pairing on the free finite-rank group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, with rational extension. It restricts on each component to its normal-transfer pairing; for cycles $a,b$ on distinct components its value is $2\operatorname{lk}(a,b)$, which need not vanish.

Suppose an embedded product cylinder $W=[-1,1]\times D^2$ meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks, on distinct components. Replace those disks by the lateral annulus and round the seams to obtain $F'$. There is an integral basis in which $B_{F'}$ has matrix $G\oplus[0]$, where $G$ is the entire matrix of $B_F$, including its cross-component entries. Thus its signature is unchanged. The boundary link and its surface collar remain fixed, so $e(F)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$, computed from boundary normal push-offs, is unchanged as well.

A finite sequence of such tubes exists making $F$ connected. All intermediate surfaces still have the original boundary link and collar, no closed components, and finite smooth disk-and-band presentations on their components. The signature and $e$ are preserved throughout.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth embedded surface with nonempty boundary and a supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentation, allowing nonorientability. Let an embedded product cylinder $W=[-1,1]\times D^2$ meet $F$ exactly in its two end disks, lying in the interior of $F$. Replace those disks by the lateral annulus $[-1,1]\times\partial D^2$ and round the two seams, leaving the rest fixed, to obtain $F'$. The normal-transfer pairing of $F'$ has the same signature as that of $F$.

More precisely, old homology basis curves can be chosen away from the two disks and extended by two classes $b,c$ to a basis for $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$ in which the new pairing matrix is
$$\begin{pmatrix}G&v&0\\v^T&k&\delta\\0&\delta&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad k\in\mathbb Z,\quad\delta\in\{1,-1\},$$
where $G$ is the old matrix. The boundary link and its entire surface collar remain fixed. In particular, for common chosen boundary normal push-offs $K_i'$ of its components $K_i$, the quantity $e(F)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$ is unchanged, as is $\operatorname{sign}(B_F)+e(F)/2$.

Assume full AC. In oriented $\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$, fix $R>2r>0$ and $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$. Let $M_\epsilon$ be the embedded Möbius band parametrized by
$$m(\theta,t)=((R+t\cos(\theta/2))\cos\theta,(R+t\cos(\theta/2))\sin\theta,-\epsilon t\sin(\theta/2)),\qquad |t|\le r,$$
with $(0,t)$ identified with $(2\pi,-t)$. Its core is oriented by increasing $\theta$. Its boundary is an unknot, its integral normal-transfer pairing is $[\epsilon]$ on the core generator, and its boundary normal framing has self-linking $2\epsilon$.

Let $F$ be any connected compact smooth embedded surface with nonempty boundary and a supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentation. Form $F'$ as the separated boundary connected sum of $F$ with a small copy of $M_\epsilon$: the two surfaces lie in disjoint ball interiors, joined along chosen boundary arcs by an untwisted product band whose interior misses them, and whose normal collar is the product of the chosen boundary normal collars. Smooth the seams. Then the boundary link of $F'$ is ambient isotopic to that of $F$, its normal pairing is integrally congruent to $B_F\oplus[\epsilon]$, and its boundary normal Euler quantity satisfies $e(F')=e(F)-2\epsilon$, where $e(S)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$ for componentwise normal push-offs determined by its surface collar. Consequently
$$\operatorname{sign}(B_{F'})+\tfrac12e(F')=\operatorname{sign}(B_F)+\tfrac12e(F).$$
Neither surface is required to be orientable, and the boundary link may have any positive number of components.

Assume full AC. Let $F_0,F_1\subset S^3$ be connected compact smooth spanning surfaces for the same nonempty link $L=K_1\cup\cdots\cup K_m$, with supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentations; neither surface need be orientable. Write $f_i(F)$ for the self-linking of a component $K_i$ with its small surface-normal push, both oriented compatibly. For arbitrary component orientations,
$$f_i(F)\equiv\sum_{j\ne i}\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_j)\pmod2.$$
In particular $f_i(F_1)-f_i(F_0)$ is even for every $i$.

By finitely many small separated crosscap additions of either sign and ambient isotopies, applied to $F_0$ and preserving its boundary link type, one obtains a connected surface $F_0^*$ with boundary literally $L$, with the same component framings as $F_1$, and with its interior disjoint from that of $F_1$ in a neighborhood of $L$. Its remaining interior intersection with the original comparison surface $F_1$ is transverse and is a finite disjoint union of embedded circles. These operations preserve $\operatorname{sign}(B_{F_0})+e(F_0)/2$, where $e(F)=-\sum_i f_i(F)$. Labels and orientations of the boundary components are transported. This is a boundary-collar normalization, not a claim that the two entire spanning surfaces are related by these moves alone.

Assume countable choice. Let $F_0,F_1\subset S^3$ be connected compact smooth surfaces with the same nonempty boundary link $L$. Suppose their interiors meet transversely in finitely many circles, and supply boundary tube charts in which their actual collars are the two positive coordinate rays. Then they are related by a finite sequence of ambient isotopies fixing $L$ pointwise and interior tube additions or removals. A tube addition replaces the two end disks of an embedded product cylinder $[-1,1]\times D^2$, whose intersection with the surface is exactly those disks, by its lateral annulus, with seam rounding; removal is its inverse. Every intermediate surface in the sequence is connected, has boundary exactly $L$, and has a finite smooth disk-and-band presentation. No orientability hypothesis is imposed. All additions can be performed before all removals, with ambient isotopies between them.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth embedded surface with nonempty boundary, possibly nonorientable, with a supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentation. The ambient three-sphere has its standard orientation. For oriented integral multicurves $a,b\subset\operatorname{int}F$, let $\tau b$ be the cycle consisting of the two small normal pushes over $b$, oriented by projection to $b$. For a one-sided circle this is one circle mapping with degree two, rather than a choice of a single normal direction. Then
$B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a well-defined symmetric integral bilinear pairing on $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, independently of representatives and sufficiently small normal pushes. Every integral homology class has an oriented multicurve representative, permitting integer coefficients. The pairing extends to rational homology, with quadratic form $q_F(x)=B_F(x,x)$ satisfying the normal-transfer linking identity.

For an embedded compact subsurface $A\subset F$ with such a finite presentation, the pairing on $A$ is the pullback of $B_F$ under inclusion. If $F$ is oriented and its boundary is one knot, its pairing has matrix $V+V^T$ in any integral basis, where $V$ is the positive-push Seifert matrix. Orientation-preserving ambient isotopies transport the pairing.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface with no closed components, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, and let $\alpha$ be a smoothly and properly embedded arc in $F$. Cut $F$ along a sufficiently small open rectangular neighborhood of $\alpha$ and round the resulting boundary corners inside $F$, obtaining $F'$. Then every component of $F'$ has nonempty boundary, the inclusion induces an injection $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)\hookrightarrow H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and its full normal-transfer pairing is the pullback of that on $F$. In particular positive or negative definiteness is preserved by this cut.

Writing $c(F)$ for the number of connected components and $b_1(F)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$, one has
$$b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+1-c(F').$$
More precisely, if the arc does not separate its component, then $c(F')=c(F)$ and $b_1(F')=b_1(F)-1$; if it separates its component, then $c(F')=c(F)+1$ and $b_1(F')=b_1(F)$. For a finite disjoint family of $m$ proper arcs, successive cuts retain the injection and pairing assertions and give $b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+m-c(F')$.

derivations.claim: Congruent finite rational matrices have isomorphic kernels, by the invertible congruence change of coordinates. The kernel of a direct sum is the direct sum of the kernels. Therefore $G\oplus[0]$ has nullity $\nu(G)+1$, while $G\oplus[\epsilon]$ for $\epsilon=\pm1$ has nullity $\nu(G)$. These statements include zero-dimensional or already singular old matrices. Ambient transport in [F5] also preserves nullity.

For the connected tube matrix in [F2], let $D=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}k&\delta\\\delta&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $C=(v,0)$. Its determinant is $-1$, and $D^{-1}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&\delta\\\delta&-k\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ since $\delta^2=1$. The invertible triangular block coordinate change eliminating $C$ gives a congruence to $(G-CD^{-1}C^T)\oplus D$. Its correction term is zero because the top-left entry of $D^{-1}$ is zero. Hence the whole matrix is congruent to $G\oplus D$, and the invertibility of $D$ proves unchanged nullity. The same equality in reverse applies to a tube removal whenever its source and target are connected. Together with step 1.1, every connected tube move, signed small crosscap and ambient isotopy in [F2] preserves nullity.

First consider two connected spanning surfaces $H_0,H_1$ for the same link. Supply their finite smooth presentations using [F1], then apply the actual normalization in [F3] to $H_0$ with $H_1$ as comparison. Each of its operations preserves nullity by step 2.1, so the normalized $H_0^*$ has the same nullity as $H_0$. Retain the boundary tubes constructed by its collar construction: the comparison collar is the angle-zero ray and the changed collar is the ray of a fixed small angle $\delta\in(0,\pi)$. The later perturbation fixes a smaller tube. The same invertible linear coordinate change in each normal plane, sending these two independent ray vectors to the two positive axes, supplies the exact collar-chart hypothesis of [F4]. These are actual whole-collar charts from the construction, not an inference merely from boundary tangent directions.

The movie in [F4] now compares $H_0^*$ and $H_1$ through connected finitely presented surfaces. At every tube addition or removal step 2.1 preserves nullity, and ambient isotopies preserve it by [F5]. Telescoping the finite equalities gives $
u(B_{H_0})=
u(B_{H_0^*})=
u(B_{H_1})$. Thus the nullity itself is independent of the connected spanning surface for the given link.

For each original $F_i$ use [F1] to join its $c(F_i)$ components by exactly $c(F_i)-1$ component-connecting tubes. Step 1.1 and the exact zero-block matrix in [F1] give a connected surface $H_i$ with $\nu(B_{H_i})=\nu(B_{F_i})+c(F_i)-1$. Apply step 4.1 to these two connected surfaces to obtain the stated invariant. This argument keeps every old cross-component entry inside $G$ at each tube connection. Ambient isotopy carries components to components and transports the pairing by [F5], so the invariant also depends only on the stated link isotopy type.

A nondegenerate pairing has nullity zero, so the equality in step 5.1 gives equal component counts for two nondegenerate spanning surfaces of the same link. A definite form is nondegenerate, including the zero-dimensional form, so this applies in particular to the two initial definite surfaces in the arc assertion. Their cut surfaces remain definite by [F5]. If their boundary links are isotopic, transport one cut surface along that isotopy and apply the same component-count equality to them. Thus the initial counts agree and the cut counts agree. The component increase is either zero or one, and is one exactly for a separating cut by [F5]; subtracting the equal initial counts from the equal final counts proves the asserted equivalence of separating arcs.

boundaries.reason: A nonempty boundary link and spanning surfaces without closed components are assumed.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement allows zero first Betti number and zero signature; no inverse of the normal form is taken.
The Statement allows a one-component link and connected or disconnected surfaces satisfy the same argument.
The Statement uses the signature, which is the difference of positive and negative ranks; the proof does not require nonsingularity.
The Statement retains the same literal boundary link, with arbitrary component orientations.
The Statement explicitly assumes full AC, which is assumed and inherited through the cited linking and smooth construction suppliers.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from the full normal-transfer pairing and its local tube/crosscap interfaces. It supplies countable choice for surface presentations, boundary normalization and the finite tube movie. Nullity calculations use finite rational linear algebra.

risk_review.notes: Preserves full disconnected and nonorientable surface scope. All new prerequisite sources and their geometric constructions still require independent owner review.

contract.proof_status_evidence: Literal local steps and scoped mechanical checks, authentic GL1978 complete-page reading receipt; independent owner mathematical review remains owed.

constructive_supplier_evidence.exact_read_body:
1.1 Choose a small normal push $K_i'$ disjoint from the whole surface $F$. Triangulate its finite disk-and-band presentation and choose arbitrary reference orientations on its finitely many triangles. Their sum modulo two is a fundamental two-chain with boundary the sum of the boundary circles modulo two. Lift that two-chain to an integral chain $C$ in $S^3\setminus K_i'$ by using the chosen triangle orientations, and orient the boundary circles as prescribed in the Statement. Then $\partial C-\sum_j K_j=2z$ for an integral one-chain $z$. Its boundary is zero, because $2\partial z=0$ and singular chain groups have no integer torsion. Applying the linking homomorphism with $K_i'$ from [F1] gives $0=\sum_j\operatorname{lk}(K_i',K_j)+2\operatorname{lk}(K_i',z)$. This use on $z$ is on complement homology and does not require it to be embedded. For $j\ne i$ the small push is homotopic to $K_i$ in the complement of $K_j$. The $i$th term is $f_i(F)$ by symmetry. Reduction modulo two proves the stated parity formula, independently of the orientability of $F$. [given, F1, construct, algebra]

1.2 A smooth boundary circle has an oriented normal disk bundle with a smooth trivialization. One may construct it on a cut parameter interval using finitely many normal frames, then correct the endpoint rotation by a smooth angle interpolation so that the frames glue; the oriented two-plane rotation group is connected. The normal exponential chart is injective at a sufficiently small uniform radius by [F4] and compactness, as in the normal-transfer construction. In these coordinates a nowhere-zero transverse vector along the circle has an angular lift on the cut interval, whose endpoint difference is $2\pi$ times an integer. Its small pushed curve is a longitude plus that many positive meridians. By [F1] its self-linking is the self-linking of the reference longitude plus this integer. In particular two such fields have the same self-linking precisely when their angular lifts differ by a periodic smooth function. Surface inward conormals and surface normals along an oriented boundary circle differ by a fixed quarter-turn in its oriented normal plane. They therefore have the same integer and the same self-linking. These assertions concern boundary collars only and do not orient the whole surface. [given, F1, F4, construct]

2.1 By step 1.1 the difference $d_i=f_i(F_1)-f_i(F_0)$ is even. If $d_i\ne0$, add $|d_i|/2$ crosscaps of sign $\epsilon=\operatorname{sign}(d_i)$ to that component of $F_0$, using [F2]. Each increases that component's self-linking by $2\epsilon$: the total Euler change is $-2\epsilon$, and the other component self-linkings are unchanged. Such a small separated attachment is available in a boundary chart, placing its Möbius band in a small ball off the surface and joining through a product collar of the chosen boundary arc. After each attachment use the local boundary-link isotopy in [F2] to return the boundary to the original $L$; linking and framings are transported by that isotopy. Use disjoint small boundary neighborhoods for the finitely many required attachments, or successive smaller neighborhoods. Connectedness and the finite disk-and-band presentation are retained. This produces a surface $\widehat F_0$ whose component framings equal those of $F_1$. [step 1.1, F2, F3, construct, algebra]

3.1 Work in disjoint sufficiently short normal tubes of the boundary circles, containing no other parts of either surface than their boundary collars. Choose the tube coordinates adapted to the actual collar of $F_1$, so it is the radial ray of angle zero. Explicitly extend its collar parametrization $c(s,x)$ slightly across $x=0$, and map $(s,x,y)$ to the short ambient normal push by $y$ of $c(s,x)$. The boundary-circle tangent, the inward collar vector and its ambient normal are independent, so [F4] gives this chart at $x=y=0$, and compactness gives a uniform tube. The finite boundary-chart extensions agree on the prescribed collar and can be patched beyond its boundary before shrinking. Thus the whole collar, rather than only its tangent line, is the angle-zero ray. On a short collar of $\widehat F_0$, the base projection to the boundary circle is a coordinate and the normal radius is a strictly increasing inward parameter. This follows at the boundary from the nonzero inward transverse derivative, then uniformly by compactness and [F4]. Thus its collar has coordinates $(s,r,\theta(s,r))$, with its angular direction tending to a smooth angle field at $r=0$. Its relative angular winding is zero by steps 1.2 and 2.1. It therefore has a periodic real angular lift on a sufficiently short collar. First straighten its angle to its limiting field on a smaller radius strip, using an angular interpolation cut off before the outer edge; then interpolate that limiting field to a fixed small angle $\delta\ne0$, again cut off in radius. Throughout these interpolations the base coordinate $s$ and radius $r$ are unchanged, so distinct parameters remain distinct and the collar stays embedded even if the angle varies in $r$. The formulas extend smoothly across $r=0$: they are rotations of the smooth transverse vector by a periodic smooth angle, while the initial straightening error vanishes with $r$. All changes vanish on an outer collar. The final innermost collar is the ray of angle $\delta$ and is disjoint from the angle-zero interior collar of $F_1$. [step 1.2, step 2.1, F4, construct]

4.1 Extend the collar embedding isotopies of step 3.1 by the unchanged embedding on the remainder of $\widehat F_0$ and use [F5]. The ambient extension fixes every boundary point because the embedding isotopy fixes it; no claim that this extension fixes the comparison surface is needed. Perform it on the finitely many disjoint boundary tubes. Denote the endpoint by $F_0'$. It still has boundary $L$, retains its component framings by [F3], and misses $F_1$ in a punctured neighborhood of each boundary component. Shrink to a common such neighborhood $U$. The given finite smooth presentation is transported by the isotopies. [step 3.1, F3, F5, F6, construct]

5.1 It remains to make the intersection outside $U$ transverse. In the boundaryless ambient manifold $S^3\setminus L$, the target $F_1\setminus L$ is a closed embedded boundaryless surface. All possible intersections of the two surfaces are contained in a compact region outside a smaller $U$. In finitely many ambient charts covering that region choose three bump-supported vector fields spanning each tangent space on smaller covering charts, with supports away from a still smaller neighborhood of $L$. Compose their short flows with parameters $a_j$, obtaining ambient diffeomorphisms $h_a$ fixed there. At zero parameter the parameter derivatives span the ambient tangent space on every possible intersection. For a sufficiently small parameter ball the same remains true at all intersections, by compactness and continuity; regions outside those covering charts retain their positive separation or are fixed. Thus the evaluation $(x,a)\mapsto h_a(x)$ from the interior of $F_0'$ is transverse to $F_1\setminus L$. Apply [F6] and choose an arbitrarily small good parameter. The path of short flows from zero to it is an ambient isotopy fixed near $L$. Its endpoint $F_0^*$ is transverse to the comparison surface outside $L$ and retains the separated collars. [step 4.1, F5, F6, construct]

6.1 Their interior intersection is now a compact one-dimensional smooth manifold with no boundary: it is transverse away from $L$ and absent in a punctured neighborhood of $L$. Compactness gives a finite cover by connected interval charts, so there are finitely many components. Each component is closed and hence compact, and [F7] makes it a smooth embedded circle. Thus only finitely many interior circles remain. Every crosscap move preserved the corrected signature by [F2], and every subsequent ambient isotopy preserved both its pairing signature and all component self-linkings by [F1] and [F3]. Their finite composition therefore preserves $\operatorname{sign}(B)+e/2$. The component labels and chosen orientations were transported throughout. This proves the claimed normalization while leaving the remaining entire-surface comparison as a separate obligation. [step 2.1, step 5.1, F1, F2, F3, F7, construct] ∎
constructive_supplier_evidence.use: Actual Proof3.1 constructs whole collar rays at angles zero and a fixed nonzero small delta; Proof5.1 fixes smaller boundary tubes during generic perturbation. The current supplier Statement only claims separated collars, so this constructive proof use is recorded separately.
